predictions.reasoning: A shift in the implied probability of one individual candidate winning an election more than three years away carries essentially no information relevant to near-term asset prices. Markets discount events on a much shorter horizon, and a 2028 primary/general outcome is far too distant and uncertain to move liquid instruments in a 12-hour window. There is no clean policy differentiation from a single Democratic contender's odds that would reprice the broad market now.

evidence_used: Market concerns the 2028 US Presidential Election, over three years away
Single-candidate probability question, not a policy or resolved outcome
No specified region/catalyst; category metadata largely missing
uncertainty_notes: Event horizon (2028) is far beyond the 12h prediction window relevance

llm_justification.summary: This market asks whether Pete Buttigieg wins the 2028 US Presidential Election—an event more than three years out involving a single candidate among many. A move in his implied probability carries no actionable, near-term information for liquid public-market assets over a 12-hour horizon. There is no reliable proxy or direction; the honest mapping is 'unclear' with very low confidence, below any tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: Asset prices discount events on horizons far shorter than 3+ years
A single early-stage candidate's odds lack differentiated market-moving policy content
No concurrent real-world catalyst is driving the market move
failure_modes: The odds shift could coincide with a genuine news event (e.g., a Democratic policy signal) that does move sectors—but attribution would be spurious
Even if directionally plausible, the magnitude cannot reach 700 bps from such a distant, diffuse signal
Broad-market proxy (SPY) is only weakly, if at all, exposed to a single 2028 candidate's odds
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
